checks.certifies: the service can complete a sampled (temperature > 0) request

negative_control.condition: the sampled path returns one malformed token
negative_control.how_produced: serve a build whose sampled path emits a single invalid token, which any parser rejects
negative_control.targets: the declared capability, not the transport

claim: Check set C was exercised against configuration example-1. Each check was observed to fail under its declared negative control. This is process evidence about the checks.
_should_be_rejected_but_is_not: A control the check fails trivially. It satisfies every requirement -- declared, executed, failed, capability-targeted, same artifact -- while establishing almost nothing, because a check that notices a malformed token may still be blind to a silently wrong answer. NCP raises the floor from 'never observed to fail' to 'observed to fail once'; it cannot raise it further, and nothing mechanical distinguishes a demanding control from a token one.
